title: Air-Fryer Beef Burger
subtitle: Homemade beef patties cooked in the air fryer
excerpt: Simple beef mince patties seasoned with salt and pepper and cooked in the air fryer until juicy inside with a lightly crisped exterior. Ready in 10 minutes from scratch.

recipe.sourceNotes: The air fryer produces a burger patty closer to a griddle-cooked result than an oven: the exterior colours quickly in the dry, circulating heat. Use beef mince with at least 15 to 20 per cent fat content: lean mince produces a dry burger. Season well just before cooking, not in advance, as salt draws out moisture. Dimple the centre of each patty to prevent it puffing up during cooking.

content.text: Handle the mince as little as possible: overworking it makes the burger dense and tough. Press the mince into patties about 2 cm thick and slightly wider than your bun, because they shrink a little during cooking. The dimple in the centre stops the patty puffing up into a dome. Season just before cooking.
Preheat the air fryer to 200 C for 3 minutes. Divide the mince into 2 portions. Press each portion into a patty about 2 cm thick. Make a shallow dimple in the centre of each patty with your thumb.
Season both sides with salt and pepper just before cooking. Place in the air fryer basket.
Cook at 200 C for 5 minutes. Flip and cook for a further 4 to 5 minutes for medium: the centre should be slightly pink. For well done, cook an additional 2 minutes.
Rest for 2 minutes. Serve in buns with lettuce, tomato, and your chosen condiments.
